content:
Apple's biggest product launch of the year is about to arrive, with more than ten new products set to debut in the short term. Below are five of the brand-new Apple products I'm most looking forward to.

iPhone Ultra

The first foldable iPhone is almost ready, and I'm really looking forward to owning a device that combines an iPhone and an iPad mini into one.

Even though hardware specs have been widely leaked, the iPhone Ultra's software is the real key to the overall experience. So I'm very curious how Apple will adapt iOS 27 to feel more native and powerful on a foldable device.

I've never used a foldable smartphone, but based on everything I've read, this product form factor seems to be the future. Apple clearly took its time before entering the foldable market, and I'm expecting it to be worth the wait.

HomePad

For years, I've been hoping Apple would take the smart home market seriously. When Mark Gurman broke the first detailed report on the upcoming "HomePad" in late 2024, it signalled that this shift was on the way.

Everything about the HomePad has me very excited. I'm looking forward to Apple Photos slideshow playback, security camera features, an AI-powered Siri, Apple Music playback with on-screen lyrics, and more.

The delays around Siri AI have pushed back the HomePad's launch much further than expected. But all signs now point to an imminent release, and I'm ready to see Apple lay out its vision for a new era of smart home devices through the HomePad and other new Home products.

All-new Apple TV 4K

The current Apple TV 4K has been out for four years. While it doesn't need an annual refresh, the rise of AI offers huge potential for a completely reinvented experience.

I'm ready to see how Siri AI, a more powerful chip, and other hardware and software upgrades combine to give the Apple TV a worthwhile upgrade.

With the camera-equipped HomePad and the new Apple TV 4K launching around the same time, I'm also curious whether earlier rumours of a camera-equipped model will come true. Being able to do FaceTime calls on the big screen without needing an iPhone would be a fantastic feature.

MacBook Ultra

I've been using the iPad Pro as my primary computer for over a decade. I made the switch in 2015 partly because Macs consistently lagged behind the iPad in adopting innovative hardware and software features.

The move to Apple Silicon chips in Macs has addressed some of those issues, and macOS is increasingly keeping pace with iOS and iPadOS. But the Mac in many ways still feels stuck in the past rather than pointing to the future.

I suspect the MacBook Ultra will change that. Adding touch support, an OLED display, the Dynamic Island, a fresh new design, and possibly even cellular connectivity would all be hugely appealing. This is the kind of Mac update I've been waiting for, and I can't wait to see what Apple delivers.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4

I still haven't decided whether to go for the Series 12 or Ultra 4 as my next watch this year. Either way, I'm very much looking forward to seeing the new models, because there's one rumoured upgrade that stands out: a new-generation S-series chip built for the AI era.

Apple Watch chip updates aren't that frequent. While Apple usually gives the S-series chip a modest bump most years, meaningful CPU performance gains only come around every three years or so. The S9 in 2023 was the last time the watch chip brought a noticeable improvement.

But there are rumours that this year's watch lineup will feature a brand-new, more powerful chip. It would be the first chip designed specifically for the AI era, and the timing couldn't be better as Siri AI rolls out.

Which upcoming Apple product are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
